first: चौ॰—जनि डरपहु मुनि सिद्ध सुरेसा। तुम्हहिँ लागि धरिहउँ नर-बेसा॥
en: 'Do not be afraid, sages, siddhas and king of the gods. For your sake I will take a human form, and with my divine parts I will be born as a man in the noble Sun dynasty.'

first: कस्यप अदिति महा तप कीन्हा। तिन्ह कहँ मैँ पूरब बर दीन्हा॥
en: 'Kashyapa and Aditi did great penance, and long ago I gave them a boon. They have now appeared in the city of Kosala as Dasharatha and Kausalya, king and queen among men.'

first: तिन्ह के गृह अवतरिहउँ जाई। रघुकुल तिलक सुचारिउ भाई॥
en: 'I will go and be born in their house as four brothers, the glory of the Raghu clan. I will make all of Narada's words come true, and I will come down with my supreme power.'

first: हरिहउँ सकल भूमि गरुआई। निर्भय होहु देव समुदाई॥
en: 'I will take away the whole weight of the earth; be free of fear, all you gods.' Hearing this divine voice from the sky, the gods turned back at once, their hearts at peace.

first: तब ब्रह्मा धरनिहि समुझावा। अभय अई मरोस जिय आवा ॥५॥
en: Then Brahma comforted the Earth; she lost her fear and felt trust in her heart.

first: दो॰—निज लोकहि बिरज्चि गे, देवन्ह इहइ सिखाइ।
en: Brahma went back to his own world after telling the gods this: 'Go down to earth, take the bodies of monkeys, and serve the feet of Hari.'

first: चौ॰—गये देव सब निज निज धामा। भूमि सहित मन कहँ बिस्रामा॥
en: All the gods went to their own homes, and the Earth too found peace of mind. The gods gladly did at once whatever Brahma had told them.

first: बनचर देइ धरी छिति माहीँ। अतुलित बल-प्रताप तिन्ह पाहीँ॥
en: They took the bodies of forest creatures on earth, with matchless strength and power. All were heroes whose weapons were rocks, trees and claws, and with steady minds they waited for Hari to come.

first: गिरि कानन जहँ तहँ महि पूरी। रहे निज निज अनीक रुचिरूरी।
en: They filled the earth everywhere, in hills and forests, each living in his own fine band. I have told all this lovely story; now hear what I left aside in the middle.

first: अवधपुरी रघुकुल-मनि राऊ। बेद बिदित तेहि दसरथ नाऊ॥
en: In Ayodhya there was a king, the jewel of the Raghu clan, named Dasharatha, famous in the Vedas. He upheld dharma, was full of virtue and wisdom, and his heart was devoted to Vishnu, who holds the bow.

first: दो॰—कौसल्यादि नारि प्रिय, सब आचरन पुनीत।
en: His dear queens, Kausalya and the others, were all pure in conduct. They loved their husband faithfully and were humble at the lotus feet of Hari.

first: चौ॰—एक बार भूपति मनमाहीँ। भइ गलानि मारे सुत नाहीँ॥
en: Once the king felt sad at heart that he had no son. At once he went to his guru's house, fell at his feet and pleaded humbly.

first: निज दुख सुख सब गुरुहि सुनायो। कहि बसिष्ठ बहु बिधि समुझायो॥
en: He told the guru all his sorrow and joy, and Vasishtha comforted him in many ways: 'Be patient; you will have four sons, famous in all three worlds, who will take away the fear of devotees.'

first: सृङ्गी रिषिहि बसिष्ठ बोलावा। पुत्रकाम सुभ जग्य करावा॥
en: Vasishtha called the sage Shringi and had him perform a holy sacrifice for the gift of sons. When the sage offered oblations with devotion, the Fire god appeared holding a dish of sacred rice pudding.

first: जो वसिष्ठ कछु हृदय विचारा। सकल काज भा सिद्ध तुम्हारा॥
en: 'Whatever Vasishtha planned in his heart, all your work is now done. King, go and share this offering among your queens in fitting portions.'

first: दो॰—तब अद्वस्य भये पावक, सकल समहि समुझाइ।
en: Then the Fire god vanished after explaining everything to the assembly. The king was lost in supreme bliss, and his heart could not hold his joy.

first: चौ॰—तबहि राय प्रिय नारि बोलाई। कौसल्यादि तहाँ चलि आई॥
en: Then the king called his dear queens, and Kausalya and the others came there. He gave half the offering to Kausalya and split the other half into two.

first: कैकेई कहँ नप सो दयऊ। रहेउ साे उभय भाग पुनि भयऊ॥
en: One of these the king gave to Kaikeyi, and what was left was again split in two. Placing these in the hands of Kausalya and Kaikeyi, he gave them to Sumitra, to everyone's content.

first: एहि बिधि गर्भ-सहित सब नारी। भईँ हृदय हरषित सुख-भारी॥
en: In this way all the queens became pregnant and felt great joy. From the day Hari entered the womb, happiness and wealth spread through all the worlds.

first: मन्दिर महँ सब राजहिँ रानी। सोभा—सील-तेज की खानी।
en: The queens, mines of beauty, goodness and radiance, shone in the palace. Some time passed happily, and then the moment came for the Lord to appear.

first: दो॰—जोग लगन ग्रह बार तिथि, सकल मये अनुकूल।
en: The yoga, the rising sign, the planets, the weekday and the lunar date all became favourable. All moving and unmoving beings were full of joy, for the birth of Rama is the root of happiness.

first: चौ॰—नवमी तिथि मधु माख पुनीता। सुकल पच्छ अभिजित हरि-प्रीता।
en: It was the holy ninth day of the bright half of the month of Chaitra, in the Abhijit hour dear to Hari. It was midday, neither cold nor hot, a sacred time that gave rest to the world.

first: सीतल मन्द सुरभि बह बाऊ। हरषित सुर सन्तन्ह मन चाऊ।
en: A cool, gentle, fragrant breeze was blowing; the gods were glad and the saints eager. The forests were in bloom, the mountains sparkled with gems, and all the rivers flowed with nectar.

first: सो अवसर बिरज्चि जब जाना। चले सकल सुर साजि विमाना॥
en: When Brahma knew the moment had come, all the gods set out in their decorated sky-chariots. The clear sky was crowded with hosts of gods, and bands of Gandharvas sang his praises.

first: बरषहिँ सुमन सुअञ्जलि साजी। गहगहि गगन दुन्दुभी बाजी॥
en: They showered flowers from cupped hands, and drums thundered in the sky. Nagas, sages and gods sang praises and offered their service in many ways.

first: दो॰—सुर-समूह बिनती करि, पहुँचे निज निज धाम।
en: After praying, the hosts of gods went back to their own homes. Then the Lord who lives in the whole world and gives rest to all the worlds appeared.

first: भये प्रगट कृपाला, दीनदयाला, काैसल्या-हितकारी।
en: The merciful Lord, kind to the humble and loving to Kausalya, appeared. The mother was filled with joy as she gazed at his wondrous form, which steals the hearts of sages.

first: लोचन अभिरामं, तनु-धन-स्यामं, निज आयुध भुज चारी।
en: His eyes were lovely and his body dark as a rain cloud, with his own weapons in his four arms. Wearing jewels and a garland of forest flowers, with large eyes, the slayer of Khara was an ocean of beauty.

first: कह दुइ कर जोरा, अस्तुति तोरी, केहि बिधि करउँ अनन्ता।
en: Joining both hands she said, 'Endless One, how can I praise you? The Vedas and Puranas say you are beyond Maya, beyond the qualities and knowledge, beyond all measure; you are an ocean of mercy and joy, home of every virtue, sung by scriptures and saints. That Lord of Lakshmi, who loves his devotees, has appeared for my good.'

first: ब्रह्मांड निकाया, निर्मित-माया, रोम रोम प्रति, बेद कहै।
en: 'The Vedas say that in every pore of your body are countless worlds made by Maya. That such a one lived in my womb is a wonder that unsettles even a steady mind.' When this knowledge rose in her, the Lord smiled, for he wished to play many parts, and told her a charming story so that she would love him as a son.

first: माता पुनि बोली, सो मति डोली, तजहु तात यह रूपा।
en: Then the mother spoke again, her mind changed: 'Dear child, give up this form and play like a baby, which is so dear to me; that joy is beyond compare.'

first: सुनि बचन सुजाना, रोदन ठाना, हाइ बालक सुर-भूपा॥
en: Hearing these words, the wise Lord of the gods became a baby and began to cry. Those who sing this story reach Hari's feet and do not fall into the well of worldly life.

first: दो॰—बिप्र-धेनु-सुर-सन्त हित, लीन्ह मनुज-अवतार।
en: For the sake of Brahmins, cows, gods and saints, the Lord took birth as a man. His body was made by his own will, and he is beyond Maya, its qualities and the senses.

first: चौ॰—सुनि सिसु रुदन परम प्रिय बानी। सम्भ्रम चलि ओई सब रानी।
en: Hearing the baby's sweet, dear cry, all the queens came hurrying. Glad maids ran here and there, and all the people of the city were lost in joy.

first: दसरथ पुत्र-जन्म सुनि काना। मानहुँ ब्रह्मानन्द समाना॥
en: When Dasharatha heard of his son's birth, he felt as if he had found the bliss of Brahman. His mind full of love and his body thrilling, he wanted to rise but first steadied himself.

first: जा कर नाम सुनत सुभ होई। माेरे गृह आवा प्रभु साेई।
en: 'The Lord whose very name brings good to those who hear it has come to my house.' His heart full of supreme joy, the king called for music to be played.

first: गुरु बसिष्ट कहें गयउ हँकारा। आये द्विजन्ह सहित नृप-द्वारा॥
en: Word was sent to Guru Vasishtha, and he came to the king's door with the Brahmins. They went and saw the matchless child, whose beauty and virtues no words can finish.

first: दो॰—तब नन्दीमुख-खाध करि, जातकरम सब कीन्ह।
en: Then the king performed the Nandimukh rite for the ancestors and all the birth ceremonies, and gave the Brahmins gold, cows, clothes and jewels.

first: चौ॰—ध्वज पताक तोरन पुर छावा। कहि न जाइ जेहि भाँति बनावा॥
en: The city was covered with flags, banners and arches, decorated beyond words. Flowers rained from the sky, and all the people were lost in the bliss of Brahman.

first: बृन्द बृन्द मिलि चलीँ लोगाई। सहज सिंगार किये उठि धाई॥
en: Women came out in groups, rushing in whatever finery they had on. Carrying golden pitchers and plates of auspicious things, they entered the king's gate singing.

first: करि आरती निछावर करहीँ। बार बार सिसु चरनन्हि परहीँ॥
en: They waved lamps, made offerings over the baby, and fell at his feet again and again. Bards, minstrels, heralds and singers sang the holy virtues of the Lord of the Raghus.

first: सरबस-दान दीन्ह सब काहू। जेहि पावा राखा नहिँ ताहू॥
en: Everyone gave away all they had, and those who received it did not keep it either. Musk, sandal and saffron made mud in the middle of every street.

first: दो॰—गृह गृह बाज बधाव सुभ, प्रगटे सुखमा-कन्द।
en: Happy music played in every house, for the root of all beauty had appeared. Men and women all over the city were full of joy.

first: चौ॰—कैकय-सुता सुमित्रा दोऊ। सुन्दर-सुत जनमत भइँ ओऊ॥
en: Kaikeyi and Sumitra too gave birth to handsome sons. Neither Sharada nor the king of serpents could describe the joy, wealth, hour and gathering of that day.

first: अवधपुरी सोहइ एहि भाँती। प्रभुहि मिलन आई जनु राती॥
en: Ayodhya looked as if Night had come to meet the Lord, but on seeing the Sun she shrank back, and yet stayed on, it seemed, as Evening.

first: अगर-धूप बहु जनु अँधियारी। उड़इ अवीर मनहुँ अरुनारी॥
en: The thick incense smoke was like darkness, and the flying red powder was like the glow of dusk. The jewels on the houses were like stars, and the golden dome on the king's palace was like the bright moon.

first: भवन बेद-धुनि अति मृदुबानी। जनु खग मुखर समय जनु सानी।
en: The soft chanting of the Vedas in the houses was like birds calling at that hour. Seeing this wonder, the Sun forgot himself, and a whole month passed without his knowing.

first: दो॰—मास दिवस कर दिवस भा, मरम न जानइ कोइ।
en: The day lasted a month, yet no one knew the secret. The Sun stood still with his chariot, so how could night come?

first: चौ॰—यह रहस्य काहू नहिँ जाना। दिन-मनि चले करत गुन गाना॥
en: No one knew this secret, and the Sun moved on, singing Rama's praises. Gods, sages and Nagas, having seen the great festival, went home praising their own luck.

first: औरउ एक कहउँ निज चोरी। सुनुगिरिजा अति दुढ़ मति ताेरी॥
en: 'Girija, let me tell you one more of my own secrets, for your mind is very firm. Kakbhushundi and I went together in human form, so that no one knew us.'

first: परमानन्द प्रेम-सुख फूले। बीथिन्ह फिरहिँ मगन मन भूले॥
en: 'Swelling with supreme bliss and love, we wandered the streets, lost in joy and forgetting ourselves. Only one whom Rama favours can know this holy deed.'

first: तेहि अवसर जो जेहि बिधि आवा। दीन्ह भूप जो जेहि मन भावा॥
en: At that time, the king gave each person who came whatever pleased his heart. He gave elephants, chariots, horses, gold, cows, diamonds and many kinds of cloth.

first: दो॰—मन सन्तोष सबन्हि के, जहँ तहँ देहिँ असीस।
en: Everyone was content and blessed them on all sides: 'May all the sons, the lords of Tulsidas, live long.'

first: चौ॰—छुक दिवस बीते एहि भाँती। जात न जानिय दिन अरु राता।
en: Some days passed like this; day and night went by unnoticed. Knowing it was time for the naming ceremony, the king sent for the wise sage.

first: करि पूजा भूपति अस भाखा। धरिय नाम जो मुनि गुनि राखा॥
en: After worshipping him, the king said, 'Sage, give them the names you have thought of.' The sage said, 'King, their names are many and matchless, but I will speak as my understanding allows.'

first: जो आनन्द-सिन्धु सुख-रासी। सीकर तें त्रैलोक सुपासी॥
en: 'He who is an ocean of bliss and a store of joy, a drop of whom comforts the three worlds, that home of happiness shall be named Rama, the giver of rest to all the worlds.'

first: बिस्व-भरन-पोषन कर जोई। ता कर नाम भरत अस होई॥
en: 'He who feeds and supports the world shall be named Bharata. He whose remembrance destroys enemies is named Shatrughna, as the Vedas make clear.'

first: दो॰—लच्छनधाम राम-प्रिय, सकल जगत आधार।
en: Guru Vasishtha gave the noble name Lakshmana to the one who is the home of good signs, dear to Rama, and the support of the whole world.

first: चौ॰—धरे नाम गुरु हृदय बिचारी। बेद-तत्व नृप तव सुत चारी॥
en: The guru chose the names with thought and said, 'King, your four sons are the essence of the Vedas.' The treasure of sages, the all of devotees, the life of Shiva, took delight in childhood play.

first: बारेहि तेँ निज हित पति जानी। लछिमन राम-चरन-रति मानी॥
en: From early childhood Lakshmana knew Rama as his master and well-wisher and loved his feet. The two brothers Bharata and Shatrughna shared the same kind of love, as of master and servant.

first: स्याम गौर सुन्दर दोउ जोरी। निरखहिँ छबि जननी तृन तोरी॥
en: The two pairs, dark and fair, were beautiful, and their mothers watched them and broke a straw to ward off the evil eye. All four were homes of good nature, beauty and virtue, yet Rama was the greatest ocean of joy.

first: हृदय अनुग्रह इन्दु प्रकासा। सूचत किरन मनोहर हासा॥
en: The moon of grace shone in his heart, and his charming smile was like its rays showing it. Sometimes in their laps, sometimes in a fine cradle, the mothers fondled him, calling him their darling.

first: दो॰—व्यापक-ब्रह्म निरञ्जन, निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद।
en: The all-pervading Brahman, stainless, without qualities and beyond all play, the unborn one, lay in Kausalya's lap, won over by love and devotion.

first: चौ॰—कामकोटि-छबि स्याम सरीरा। नीलकज बारिद गम्भीरा॥
en: His dark body had the beauty of millions of Love gods, deep like a blue lotus or a rain cloud. His rosy lotus feet had shining nails, like pearls sitting on lotus petals.

first: रेख कुलिस ध्वज अङ्कुस साेहै। नूपुर धुनि सुनि मुनि मन मोहै॥
en: The marks of thunderbolt, flag and goad shone on his soles, and the sound of his anklets charmed the sages. A belt of little bells was round his waist, there were three folds on his belly, and his navel was so deep that only one who has seen it knows.

first: भुज बिसाल भूषन जुत भूरी। हिय हरि-नख अति सोभा रुरी॥
en: His long arms wore many ornaments, and a tiger-claw charm shone on his chest. The necklace of gems and its pendant gleamed on his breast, and the mark of the Brahmin's foot there charmed the mind.

first: कम्बु कंठ अति चिबुक सुहाई। आनन अमित मदन-छबि छाई॥
en: His neck was like a conch and his chin very lovely, and his face shone with the beauty of countless Love gods. Who can describe his two little teeth above and below, his red lips, his nose and the mark on his brow?

first: सुन्दर स्रवन सुचारु कपोला। अति प्रिय मधुर ताेतरे बोला॥
en: He had lovely ears and fine cheeks, and his sweet lisping baby talk was very dear. His mother combed and arranged his glossy, curly birth-hair in many ways.

first: पीत झँगुलिया तनु पहिराई। जानु-पानि विचरनि माेहि भाई॥
en: She dressed him in a little yellow frock, and his crawling on knees and hands pleases me. Even the Vedas and Shesha cannot describe his form; only those who have seen it, even in a dream, know it.

first: दो॰—सुख सन्दोह माेह पर, ज्ञान-गिरा-गोतीत।
en: The Lord, full of joy, beyond delusion, and beyond knowledge, speech and senses, was won by the deep love of the royal couple and played holy childhood games.

first: चौ॰—एहि बिधि राम जगत-पितु-माता। कोसलपुरबासिन्ह सुख-दाता॥
en: So Rama, the father and mother of the world, gave joy to the people of Kosala. Bhavani, this is clearly the reward of those who love the feet of the Lord of the Raghus.

first: रघुपत्ति-बिमुख जतन कर कोरा। कवन सकइ भव-बन्धन छोरी॥
en: One who turns away from Rama may try ten million ways, but who can untie the bonds of worldly life? Even Maya, who holds all moving and unmoving beings in her power, fears the Lord.

first: भृकुटि-बिलास नचावइ ताही। अस प्रभु छाडि भजिय कहु काही॥
en: He makes her dance with a play of his brows; tell me, leaving such a Lord, whom should one worship? Give up cleverness and worship him in thought, deed and word, and the Lord of the Raghus will show mercy.

first: एहि बिधि सिसु-बिनोद प्रभु कीन्हा। सकल नगर-बासिन्ह सुख दीन्हा॥
en: So the Lord played as a child and gave joy to the whole city. Sometimes the mother took him in her lap and rocked him, and sometimes laid him in the cradle and swung it.

first: दो॰—प्रेम मगन कौसल्या, निसि दिन जात न जान।
en: Kausalya was so lost in love that she did not notice night and day pass. Lost in love for her son, she sang of his childhood deeds.

first: चौ॰—एक बार जननी अन्हवाये। करि सिंगार पलना पौढ़ाये॥
en: Once the mother bathed him, dressed him and laid him in the cradle. Then she bathed to worship the Lord, the chosen deity of her family.

first: करि पूजा नैवेद चढ़ावा। आपु गई जहँ पाक बनावा॥
en: After the worship she offered food, and went to where the meals were cooked. When she came back there, she saw her son eating the offering.

first: गह जननी सिसु पहिँ भयभीता। देखा बाल तहाँ पुनि सूता॥
en: Frightened, the mother went to the child and found him asleep there. Coming back again, she saw the same son eating; her heart trembled and she could not calm herself.

first: इहाँ उहाँ दुइ बालक देखा। मति भ्रम माेर कि आन बिसेखा॥
en: She had seen two boys, one here and one there: 'Is my mind confused, or is this something more?' Seeing his mother upset, the Lord Rama gave a sweet smile.

first: दो॰—देखरावा मातहि निज, अदभुत रूप अखंड।
en: He showed his mother his wonderful, complete form, with millions upon millions of universes on every hair of his body.

first: चौ॰—अगनितरविससिसिवचतुरानन। बहुगिरिसरितसिन्धुमहिकानन॥
en: Countless suns, moons, Shivas and Brahmas, many mountains, rivers, seas, lands and forests; time, karma, the qualities, knowledge and nature: she saw even what she had never heard of.

first: देखी माया सब बिधि गाढ़ी अति सभीत जोरे कर ठाढ़ी॥
en: She saw mighty Maya standing in great fear with joined hands. She saw the soul that Maya makes dance, and the devotion that sets it free.

first: तन पुलकित मुख बचन न आवा। नयन मूँदि चरनन्हि सिर नावा॥
en: Her body thrilled, no words came from her mouth, and she closed her eyes and bowed her head at his feet. Seeing his mother amazed, the slayer of Khara became a baby again.

first: अस्तुति करि न जाइ भय माना। जगत-पिता मैँ सुत करि जाना॥
en: Struck with fear, she could not praise him: 'I took the Father of the world for my son.' Hari comforted his mother in many ways: 'Listen, mother, do not tell this to anyone.'

first: दो॰—बार बार कौसल्या, बिनय करइ कर जोरि।
en: Again and again Kausalya pleaded with joined hands, 'Lord, may your Maya never touch me again.'

first: चौ॰—बाल चरितहरिबहु बिधि कीन्हा। अति अनन्द दासन्ह कहँ दीन्हा॥
en: Hari played many childhood games and gave great joy to his servants. After some time all the brothers grew bigger, delighting their family.

first: चूड़ाकरन कीन्ह गुरु जाई। बिप्रन्ह पुनि दछिना बहु पाई॥
en: The guru came and performed their first-haircut ceremony, and the Brahmins again received many gifts. The four lovely princes went about doing countless charming deeds.

first: मन-क्रम-बचन अगोचर जाई। दसरथ-अजिर बिचर प्रभु सोई॥
en: The Lord who is beyond the reach of thought, deed and word wandered in Dasharatha's courtyard. When the king sat down to eat, the boy would not leave his playmates and come.

first: कौसल्या जब बोलन जाई। ठुमुक ठुमुक प्रभु चलहिँ पराई॥
en: When Kausalya went to call him, the Lord ran away with tottering steps. He whom the Vedas call 'not this' and whose end Shiva could not find, the mother ran to catch by force.

first: धूसर धूरि भरे तनु आये। भूपति बिहँसि गोद बैठाये ॥५॥
en: He came back with his body covered in dust, and the king smiled and sat him on his lap.

first: दो॰—भोजन करत चपल चित, इत उत अवसर पाइ।
en: While eating, his mind was restless; finding a chance, he ran off this way and that, laughing, his face smeared with curd and rice.

first: चौ॰—बालचरित अति सरल सुहाये। सारद सेष सम्भु स्त्रुति गाये॥
en: These simple, charming childhood deeds have been sung by Sharada, Shesha, Shambhu and the Vedas. Those whose minds do not love them have been cheated by fate.

first: भये कुमार जबहिँ सब भ्राता। दीन्ह जनेऊ गुरु-पितु-माता॥
en: When the brothers were old enough, the guru and parents gave them the sacred thread. The Lord of the Raghus went to the guru's house to study, and learned every subject in a short time.

first: जाकी सहज स्वास स्त्रुति चारी। सो हरि पढ़ यह कौतुक भारी॥
en: He whose natural breath is the four Vedas went to study: a great play indeed! Skilled in learning and humility, full of virtue, they played all the games of princes.

first: करतल बान धनुष अति साेहा। देखत रूप चराचर मोहा॥
en: With bows and arrows in their hands they looked splendid, and all creation was charmed by their form. In whatever streets the brothers walked, men and women stood still in wonder.

first: दो॰—कोसलपुर-बासी नर, नारि बृद्ध अरु बाल।
en: To all the people of Kosala, men and women, old and young, gracious Rama was dearer than life.

first: चौ॰—बन्धु सखा सँग लेहिँ बोलाई। बन मृगया नित खेलहिँ जाई॥
en: He would call his brothers and friends and go to the forest every day to hunt. He shot only animals fit for sacrifice, after thought, and brought them each day to show the king.

first: जे मृग राम बान के मारे। ते तनु तजि सुरलोक सिधारे॥
en: The deer killed by Rama's arrows left their bodies and went to heaven. He ate with his brothers and friends and followed his parents' orders.

first: जेहि बिधि सुखी होहिँ पुर लोगा। करहिँ कृपानिधि सेाइ सञ्जोगा॥
en: The ocean of mercy did whatever would make the people happy. He listened closely to the Vedas and Puranas and then explained them to his brothers.

first: प्रातकाल उठि कै रघुनाथा। मातु पिता गुरु नावहिँ माथा॥
en: Rising at dawn, the Lord of the Raghus bowed his head to his mother, father and guru. With their leave he did the city's work, and the king rejoiced to see his conduct.

first: दो॰—व्यापक अकल अनीह अज, निर्गुन नाम न रूप।
en: The all-pervading one, without parts, desires or birth, without qualities, name or form, does many matchless deeds for the sake of his devotees.

first: चौ॰—यह सब चरित कहा मैँ गाई। आगिल कथा सुनहु मन लाई॥
en: I have sung all these deeds; now listen closely to the story that follows. The great and wise sage Vishvamitra lived in a forest, knowing it to be a holy place for his hermitage.

first: जहँ जप जोग जज्ञ मुनि करहीँ। अति मारीच सुबाहुहि डरहीँ॥
en: There the sages did their prayers, yoga and sacrifices, but they greatly feared Maricha and Subahu. As soon as the demons saw a sacrifice they rushed in and caused havoc, and the sages suffered.

first: गाधि-तनय मन चिन्ता ब्यापी। हरि विनु मरहिँ न निसिचर पापी॥
en: The son of Gadhi was worried: 'These wicked demons will not die without Hari.' Then the great sage thought, 'The Lord has been born to remove the earth's burden.'

first: एहू मिस देखउँ पद जाई। करि बिनती आनउँ दोउ भाई॥
en: 'With this as my reason I will go and see his feet, and by pleading I will bring back the two brothers. I will see with my own eyes the Lord who is the home of knowledge, detachment and every virtue.'

first: दो॰—बहु बिधि करत मनोरथ, जात लागि नहिँ बार।
en: Making many such wishes, he did not take long on the way. After bathing in the Sarayu, he went to the king's court.

first: चा॰—मुनि आगमन सुना जब राजा। मिलन गयउ लेइ बिप्र समाजा॥
en: When the king heard that the sage had come, he went with the Brahmins to meet him. He bowed to the ground, honoured him, and seated him on his own seat.

first: चरन पखारि कीन्हि अति पूजा। मो सम आजु धन्य नहिँ दूजा॥
en: He washed his feet and worshipped him fully: 'No one is as blessed as I am today.' He served him many kinds of food, and the great sage was very glad at heart.

first: पुनि चरनन्हि मेले सुत चारी। राम देखि मुनि देह बिसारी॥
en: Then the king laid his four sons at his feet. Seeing Rama, the sage forgot his body, lost in the beauty of his face like a chakor bird drawn to the full moon.

first: तब मन हरषि बचन कह राऊ। मुनि अस कृपा न कीन्हेहु काऊ॥
en: Then the king, glad at heart, said, 'Sage, you have never shown such kindness before. Why have you come? Tell me, and I will not delay in doing it.'

first: असुर समूह सतावहिँ माही। मैं जाचन आयउँ नृप तोही॥
en: 'Hordes of demons trouble me, king, and I have come to ask you for something. Give me Rama with his brother; when the demons are killed, I will be safe.'

first: दो॰—देहु भूप मन हरषित, तजहु माह अज्ञान।
en: 'Give them gladly, king, and give up attachment and ignorance. For you, lord, it will bring merit and fame, and for them great good.'

first: चौ॰—सुनि राजा अतिअप्रिय बानी। हृदय-कम्प मुख-दुति-कुम्हिलानी।
en: Hearing these very unwelcome words, the king's heart shook and the glow left his face. 'I got four sons in my old age; Brahmin, you have not spoken with thought.'

first: माँगहु भूमि धेनु धन कोसा। सरबस देउँ आजु सहरोसा॥
en: 'Ask for land, cows, wealth or treasure, and I will gladly give you everything today. Nothing is dearer than body and life, and even those, sage, I would give in a moment.'

first: सब सुत प्रिय माेहि प्रान कि नाँई। राम देत नहिँ बनइ गेसाँई॥
en: 'All my sons are dear to me as life, but master, I cannot give Rama. Where are the terrible, cruel demons, and where my lovely young son?'

first: सुनि नृप-गिरा प्रेम-रस-सानी। हृदय हरष माना मुनि ज्ञानी॥
en: Hearing the king's words, soaked in love, the wise sage was glad at heart. Then Vasishtha explained things to the king in many ways, and his doubt was gone.

first: अति आदर दोउ तनय बोलाये। हृदय लाइ बहु भाँति सिखाये॥
en: With great affection the king called the two sons, embraced them and gave them much advice. 'Sage, these two sons are my very life; now you are their father, and no one else.'

first: दो॰—सौँपे भूप रिषिहि सुत, बहु बिधि देइ असीस।
en: The king handed his sons to the sage with many blessings. The Lord went to his mother's palace, bowed his head at her feet, and set off.

first: सो॰—पुरुष सिंह दोउ बीर, हरषि चले मुनि भय हरन।
en: The two heroes, lions among men, set out gladly to remove the sage's fear. They are oceans of mercy, steady of mind, the cause and maker of the whole universe.

first: चौ॰—अरुन नयन उर बाहु बिसाला। नील जलद तनु स्याम तमाला॥
en: Their eyes were rosy, chests broad and arms long, and Rama's body was dark like a blue cloud or a tamal tree. Yellow cloth and fine quivers were tied at their waists, and they held lovely bows and arrows in their hands.

first: स्याम गौर सुन्दर दोउ भाई। बिस्वामित्र महानिधि पाई॥
en: In the two lovely brothers, dark and fair, Vishvamitra had found a great treasure. 'I know the Lord is devoted to Brahmins; for my sake he has left his father.'

first: चले जात मुनि दीन्हि देखाई। सुनि ताड़का क्रोध करि धाई॥
en: As they went, the sage pointed out Tadaka, and hearing them she rushed at them in anger. With a single arrow Rama took her life, and knowing her wretched, he gave her a place in his own abode.

first: तब रिषिनिज-नाथहि जिय चीन्ही। बिद्यानिधि कहँ बिद्या दीन्ही॥
en: Then the sage, knowing him in his heart as his own Lord, gave knowledge to the treasure of knowledge: a skill that keeps away hunger and thirst and gives the body matchless strength and radiance.

first: दो॰—आयुध सर्ब समर्पि कै, प्रभु निज आस्त्रम आनि।
en: Handing over all his weapons, the sage brought the Lord to his hermitage and, knowing him to love devotion, fed him roots, bulbs and fruit.

first: चौ॰—प्रात कहा मुनि सन रघुराई। निर्भय जज्ञ करहु तुम्ह जाई॥
en: In the morning the Lord of the Raghus said to the sage, 'Go and perform your sacrifice without fear.' All the sages began their fire offerings, and he himself stood guard over the sacrifice.

first: सुनि मारीच निसाचर काेही। लेइ सहाय धावा मुनि-द्रोही॥
en: Hearing this, the angry demon Maricha, enemy of sages, rushed in with helpers. Rama struck him with an arrow without a point, and he was thrown a hundred yojanas, across the sea.

first: पावक-सर सुबाहु पुनि जारा। अनुज निसाचर कटक सँघारा॥
en: Then he burned Subahu with a fire arrow, and his younger brother destroyed the demon army. Having killed the demons and freed the Brahmins from fear, he was praised by all the gods and sages.

first: तहँ पुनि कछुक दिवस रघुराया। रहे कोन्हि बिप्रन्ह पर दाया॥
en: The Lord of the Raghus stayed there some more days, showing kindness to the Brahmins. Out of devotion the Brahmins told him many old stories, though the Lord knew them all.

first: तब मुनि सादर कहा बुझाई । चरित एक प्रभु देखिय जाई॥
en: Then the sage said respectfully, 'Lord, come and see a certain event.' Hearing of the bow sacrifice, the lord of the Raghu clan gladly went with the great sage.

first: आस्त्रम एक दीख मग माहीँ। खग मृग जीव जन्तु तहँ नाहीँ॥
en: On the way he saw a hermitage with no birds, beasts or creatures of any kind. Seeing a stone there, the Lord asked the sage, and the sage told him the whole story in detail.

first: दो॰—गौतम-नारि साप बस, उपल देह धरि धीर।
en: 'Gautama's wife, under a curse, has taken a body of stone and waits patiently, longing for the dust of your lotus feet. Show her mercy, hero of the Raghus.'

first: परसत पद-पावन, सोक नसावन, प्रगट भई तप,-पुज्ज सही।
en: At the touch of his holy feet that end all sorrow, she appeared, truly a mass of penance. Seeing the Lord of the Raghus, giver of joy to his people, she stood before him with joined hands.

first: अति प्रेम अधीरा, पुलक-सरीरा, मुख नहिँ आवइ, बचन कही।
en: Overcome by love, her body thrilling, she could not say a word. Most fortunate, she clung to his feet, and tears streamed from both her eyes.

first: धीरज मन कीन्हा, प्रभु कहँ चीन्हा, रघुपति कृपा भगति पाई।
en: She steadied her mind, knew the Lord, and by his grace gained devotion; then in very pure words she began to praise him: 'Glory to you, Lord of the Raghus, known through true knowledge! I am an impure woman, and you purify the world, enemy of Ravana and joy of your people; lotus-eyed one who frees from the fear of the world, protect me, protect me, I have come to you for refuge.'

first: मुनि साप जो दीन्हा, अति भल कीन्हा, परम अनुग्रह, मैँ माना।
en: 'The sage did well to curse me, and I take it as the greatest kindness, for I have seen with full eyes Hari who frees from the world, and Shankar knows this as the only real gain. Lord, I am very simple; this is my prayer: I ask no other boon, only that my mind, like a bee, may lovingly drink the pollen of your lotus feet.'

first: जेहि पद सुरसरिता, परम पुनीता, प्रगट भई सिव,-सीस धरी।
en: 'The feet from which the holy Ganga came, whom Shiva bears on his head, the lotus feet that Brahma worships, the kind Lord Hari has placed on my head.' So Gautama's wife fell again and again at Hari's feet, received the boon her heart desired, and went full of joy to her husband's world.

first: दो॰—अस प्रभु दीनबन्धु हरि, कारन रहित दयाल।
en: Such is the Lord Hari, friend of the humble, kind without any reason. Foolish Tulsidas, give up deceit and worldly tangles and worship him.
